notes:
CONFLICT, two defects in one clause line, both in the same direction. Not resolved here.

SysML 8.2.2.17.4 states:
    SendNode : SendActionUsage =
    OccurrenceUsagePrefix ActionUsageDeclaration? 'send'
    ( ownedRelationship += NodeParameterMember SenderReceiverPart?
    | ownedRelationship += EmptyParameterMember SendReceiverPart )?
    ActionBody

vendor/pilot/SysML.xtext:1499 states:
    OccurrenceUsagePrefix ActionNodeUsageDeclaration? 'send'
    ( ActionBody
    | ( => ( ownedRelationship += NodeParameterMember SenderReceiverPart?
           | ownedRelationship += EmptyParameterMember SenderReceiverPart )
          ActionBody ) )

FIRST DISAGREEMENT - SendReceiverPart. The clause's second alternative ends in
SendReceiverPart. That name is defined nowhere in either specification: a search
of the whole clause export finds it in this one line and in no header. The
Xtext writes SenderReceiverPart in the same position, and SenderReceiverPart IS
defined, two lines below in this very clause. A rule referencing an undefined
nonterminal cannot be derived, so this one is not a difference that can be left
standing either way.

SECOND DISAGREEMENT - which declaration. The clause writes
ActionUsageDeclaration?, the Xtext ActionNodeUsageDeclaration?. These are
different languages, not two names for one rule:
    ActionUsageDeclaration : ActionUsage = UsageDeclaration ValuePart?   (8.2.2.17.2)
    ActionNodeUsageDeclaration : ActionUsage = 'action' UsageDeclaration?  (8.2.2.17.2)
The first has no 'action' keyword and so would admit `name send x to y;`; the
second requires it and admits `action name send x to y;`. Three things side with
the Xtext, including the specification against itself: SendNodeDeclaration, in
this same clause and covering the same ground, writes `ActionNodeUsageDeclaration?
'send' ...`; AcceptNode reaches AcceptNodeDeclaration's ActionNodeUsageDeclaration?;
and AssignmentNodeDeclaration writes ( ActionNodeUsageDeclaration )?. SendNode's
line is the only one of the four that differs.

NOT A DISAGREEMENT, for the record: the Xtext's ( ActionBody | ( => (...) ActionBody ) )
is the clause's ( ... )? ActionBody with the optionality hoisted into an explicit
choice and a '=>' syntactic predicate added to steer the parser generator. That is
an LL workaround and must not be ported whichever way the two questions above are
resolved; the clause's ( ... )? ActionBody is the form to keep.

No corpus instance separates the two readings: every send in the pinned corpus
writes no declaration at all before 'send', so the optional part is absent and
both readings accept all of them. The corpus cannot adjudicate this.

For the adjudicator: both questions, and whether each needs an entry in
deviations.json. The misspelling looks like the InstatiatedTypeMember and
PrefixMetadataMember class already recorded there; whether either is filed on the
OMG tracker has NOT been searched, and no issue number is cited on either.
